TfOH-catalyzed domino cycloisomerization/hydrolytic 
defluorination of 2,3-allenyl perfluoroalkyl ketones 
Can Xue, Xin Huang, Shangze Wu, Jing Zhou, Jianxin Dai, Chunling Fu, and Shengming Ma* 
A unique TfOH-catalyzed domino cycloisomerization/h ydrolytic 
defluorination reaction of easily available n-perfluoroalkyl 
allenones in the presence of H 2O providing furanyl perfluoroalkyl 
ketones has been developed. The 18 O-labelling experiments 
confirmed that the oxygen atom of the carbonyl grou p in the final 
products originates from water. 
Furans are ubiquitous heterocycles, widely existed in naturally 
occurring and biologically active compounds 1 and materials, 2 
and have been applied as versatile building blocks in organic 
synthesis. 3 There are two general approaches commonly used 
for the preparation of these five0membered rings: 
functionalization of a pre0formed heterocyclic core
4 and 
assembly of the ring from acyclic precursors. 5 Considering the 
unique structure and substituent0loading capability , multi0
substituted furans can be conveniently formed from transition 
metal0catalyzed cyclization (such as Au, Ag, Rh, Pd , etc.) of 
allenones 6010  (Scheme 1): Marshall  et al.  reported the Ag +0 or 
Rh +0catalyzed cycloisomerization of allenones to affor d tri0
substituted furans; 6 Hashmi and Alcaide found that Pd(II) was 
also a proper catalyst in this conversion; 7 Hashmi, Che, and 
later Alcaide developed Au0catalyzed cycloisomeriza tion of 
allenones; 8 Gevorgyan’s group had systematically studied the 
cascade 1,20migration/cyclization of allenones subs trates or 
intermediates under the catalytic of several transi tion metal 
catalysts. 9 Previously, we and Wang’s group have demonstrated 
efficient synthetic routes for the preparation of m ulti0
substituted furans via the Pd0catalyzed cross0coupl ing 
cyclization of 2,30allenones with aryl halides, all ylic halides or 
arylboronic acids, respectively. 10   
 On the other hand, due to the mimic effect and ver y high 
electronegativity, the introduction of fluorine ato ms into 
organic molecules would significantly change their properties, 
such as solubility, bioavailability, and metabolic stability. 11  
Because of these special properties, fluorine conta ining 
compounds are of great importance and extensively a pplied in 
agricultural, pharmaceuticals, and materials scienc e. 12  However, 
to the best of our knowledge there is no synthetic methodology 
reported for generating perfluoroalkyl substituted furans. Due 
to the fact that transition metal catalysts are usu ally expensive 
and toxic, here, we wish to report the metal0free T fOH0
catalyzed 13  domino cycloisomerization of allenyl perfluoroalky l 
ketones, which could be easily prepared according t o the 
method developed in this group, 14  followed by hydrolytic 
defluorinaiton to yield furan020yl perfluoroalkyl k etones 
efficiently (Scheme 1).

 We were studying the cyclization of easily availab le diaryl0
substituted 1a  firstly with transition metal catalysts. Although 
perfluoroalkyl furan 2a  could be obtained in 46% NMR yield 
under the catalysis of AuCl 3 (entry 1, Table 1), no reaction 
occurred when AuCl, Au(PPh 3)OTf, 9g  AgBF 4,9c  and AgOTf 9g,9h  
were attempted as the catalysts (entries 205, Table  1). 
Furthermore, we explored such a conversion with dif ferent 
metallic trifluoromethanesulfonates, which provided  us with 
very interesting results: when aged Sc(OTf) 3 was used as the 
catalyst, instead of perfluoroalkylfuran 2a , an unexpected more 
polar product, which was finally identified as 4,50 diphenyl030
propylfuran020yl perfluoropropyl ketone 3a  by the 1H, 13 C, 19 F 
NMR, NOE, IR, MS and elemental analysis together wi th X0
Ray single crystal diffraction data (Figure S1), 15  was obtained 
(entry 6, Table 1); neither newly purchased CuOTf·P hH nor

and 98% recovery of 1a , respectively (entries 7 and 8, Table 1); 
no reaction took place in the O 2 atmosphere (entry 9, Table 1); 
considering that the aged Sc(OTf) 3 may contain TfOH, we tried 
to add 1.5 equiv of H 2O to the reaction vessel. To our delight, 
67 % of 2a  and 27% of 3a were obtained (entry 10, Table 1). 
Then, TfOH was tested as the sole catalyst: using a ged TfOH 
(10 mol%), which may also contain water, afforded a  mixture 
of 2a  and  3a (entry 11, Table 1).

 Moreover, we varied the loading of water. Even in the 
absence of any added water, the reaction could stil l form 3a  in a 
decent yield (entry 1, Table S1), while a high load ing of H 2O 
(up to 100 equiv) stopped the conversion (entry 9, Table S1). 
By comparing entry 2 with entry 3 of Table S1, redu cing the 
dosage of TfOH to 5 mol% would yield a mixture of 2a  (88%) 
and 3a  (12%) at 60 oC with an extended reaction time as 
determined by the 1H NMR analysis of the crude product. In the 
end, 1.8 equiv of H 2O came out to be the best choice (entry 5, 
Table S1).  
 With the optimized reaction conditions in hand, we  then 
explored the scope of this transformation: the reac tion of 1,10
diphenyl0substituted allenyl perfluoroalkyl ketones  
1a-1c  
proceeded to afford ketone 3 with excellent yields no matter R 3 
is a propyl or a methyl group and R f is a perfluoropropyl or a 
perfluoropentyl group (entries 103, Table 2). When a methyl 
group took the place of the phenyl group as R 2, the 1,20Ph shift 
product 3d  was produced exclusively (entry 4, Table 2). 
Furthermore, 1,20 iPr migrated product 3f was also formed 
(entry 6, Table 2). Interestingly,  exclusive 1,20iPr migration was 
observed affording 3e  in a moderate yield with R 1 = iso 0propyl 
and R 2 = methyl (entry 5, Table 2). When R 1 = H and R 2 = Ph 
the tandem reactions could all proceed smoothly to afford 1,20H 
shift products no matter R 3 was a propyl, an ethyl, or a methyl 
group (entries 7010, Table 2). The substituent of t he aryl group 
has almost no significant effect on the reaction (e ntries 11 and 
12, Table 2). Albeit with a lower yield, 20thienyl group may 
also be compatible in this conversion (entry 13, Ta ble 2). To 
demonstrate the practicality of the procedure, a gr am scale (3.0 
mmol) reaction of 1g  was also conducted in moderate yield 
(63%) as shown in entry 8, Table 2.

 The furanyl perfluoroalkyl ketone 3 producted here have 
been demonstrated to be very useful in organic synt hesis as 
shown in Scheme 2: when 3a  was treated with MeLi in Et 2O at 
060 oC for 14 h, perfluoropropyl containing tertiary alc ohol 4a  
could be obtained in 80% isolated yield 14  while secondary 
alcohol  5a was afforded efficiently with DIBAL0H as the 
reducing reagent.

presence of water and TfOH from 1a  (entry 6, Table 1), 2a  was

(1.0 equiv) and a catalytic amount of TfOH (10 mol% ) in 
toluene at 100 oC for 2 h afforded 3a  successfully in 97% 
isolated yield (eq. 1). Thus, 2a  has been demonstrated to be the 
key intermediate to form 3a  from 1a . 
 
 Furthermore, 18 O0labeling experiments were conducted: 20
perfluorobutyl050(40methylphenyl)030propylfuran 2j  could be 
obtained in 98% isolated yield from 1j  with AuCl (5 mol%) in 
toluene at 100 oC for 12 h, then 2j  was treated with TfOH (5 
mol%) and H 2
18 O (1.5 equiv) in toluene for 12 h to afford  3j 0
18 O in 81% yield and 65.8% 18 O (Path a, Scheme 3); in the 
sequential two0step one0pot conversion, 1j  was treated firstly 
with AuCl (5 mol%) in toluene at 100 oC for 12 h, which was 
followed by the direct addition of TfOH (5 mol%) to gether with 
H2
18 O (1.5 equiv) in toluene at 100 oC for another 12 h to 
provide 3j 018 O in 75% yield with 56.6% 18 O for two steps (Path 
b, Scheme 3). Hence, it is confirmed that the oxyge n atom of 
the carbonyl group originated from water. 
 
Scheme 3. 18 O0labeling experiments. 
 Based on these results a possible mechanism is pre sented: 
In the presence of TfOH, the allene moiety of 1a  would interact 
with H + followed by nucleophilic attack from the carbonyl 
oxygen to form the cyclic oxonium intermediate M1 . 1,20
Phenyl shift of the resonance structure M2  would form M3 . 
Aromatization would provide the tetra0substituted f uran 2a  by 
releasing the catalytically active species H + (Cycle A, Scheme 
4). The in0situ formed product 2a  would then react with H + in 
tandem to afford the oxonium intermediate M4 , which would 
undergo the elimination of HF to afford M5 . Subsequent 
nucleophilic attack of water with M5  would form M6 . 
Elimination of HF would finally yield 3a  (Cycle B, Scheme 
4). 16 
In conclusion, we have identified H + for the first time as 
the catalyst for the novel domino cycloisomerizatio n/hydrolytic 
defluorination of allenyl perfluoroalkyl ketones. I n the presence 
of water, such a metal0free tandem TfOH0catalyzed r eaction 
would efficiently conceive furan020yl perfluoroalkyl ketones, of 
which the carbonyl oxygen originated from water as confirmed 
by 18 O0labelling experiments. The selectivity of 1,20shi ft has 
been established: H > Ar > secondary alkyl >primary  alkyl. 
Considering the readily availability of the startin g materials 14 
and the potential of these perfluoroalkyl0containin g furanyl 
ketones, this method will be useful in organic chem istry, 
materials sciences, and medicinal chemistry. Furthe r studies in 
this area are still undergoing in our laboratory.
